title: ELT site testing: Cerro Armazones by night
caption: Cerro Armazones at night, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This night view shows Cerro Armazones, a mountain in Chile not far from ESO's Paranal Observatory, home of the flagship Very Large Telescope. The mountain was one of the places considered for the future Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), which, with a mirror in the 40-meter class, is set to be the world's biggest eye on the sky.

The ELT program office studied half a dozen potential sites. Sky quality was only part of the picture. The choice also weighed wider scientific factors and practical needs for building and running an observatory, such as access, water and power supplies, and political stability.

Cerro Armazones made the final short list of the ELT Site Selection Advisory Committee and was its preferred site. It offered the best balance of sky quality across all the factors considered, and it could be run in an integrated way with the existing Paranal Observatory.

understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the mountain and sky may look brighter here than they would at night in person.
